instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: B2B SaaS platform for field service management including scheduling, dispatching, mobile work orders, and invoicing. 600+ customers across HVAC, plumbing, and electrical trades. Processing 2 million work orders annually. Current ARR growth rate of 40%. Evaluating AI-powered route optimization and parts inventory prediction modules. We operate across multiple locations and have distinct functional leadership for operations, commercial, finance, and technology. Our annual planning process is well-established but can be rigid — mid-cycle innovation funding requires navigating a formal business case approval chain involving 3-4 stakeholders.
answers.pastInitiatives: Our engineering team adopted an agile methodology last year, moving from waterfall-style quarterly releases to 2-week sprints with continuous deployment. This reduced our release cycle time by 60% and improved cross-functional collaboration. However, adjacent teams (marketing, support) are still adapting to the faster cadence.
answers.strategicGoals: We operate in a consolidating market where competitors are merging to gain economies of scale. Our independent position is increasingly vulnerable. We need to proactively strengthen our competitive positioning — either by deepening our specialization in high-margin niches where scale matters less, or by building platform-like switching costs that make our offering stickier for existing customers.
answers.teamSize: We have a dedicated innovation squad of 8 people — 4 engineers, 1 data scientist, 1 UX designer, 1 product manager, and a part-time business analyst. This team operates with its own sprint cadence separate from the core product teams and has an allocated annual innovation budget. They report progress quarterly to the executive committee.
answers.additionalContext: We completed a merger with a similarly-sized competitor 4 months ago and are in the middle of integrating teams, systems, and processes. The combined organization has significant duplication — two CRMs, two HR systems, overlapping product lines. There is a unique window to redesign processes from scratch rather than patching legacy approaches, but cultural integration is fragile and change fatigue is real.

input.changes_since_last: Acquired 8 new enterprise clients. Expanded into adjacent market. Digital maturity improving.

opportunities.title: Develop Platform Stickiness via Niche Specialization
opportunities.rationale: The market defense strategy requires making the offering less replaceable. Focus should shift from general platform features to deep specialization in high-margin niches (e.g., specific industrial compliance reporting) that increases switching costs for enterprise clients.

first_actions: Conduct a specialized gap analysis comparing current regulatory compliance capabilities against the top 3 target niche standards.
Integrate mandatory compliance workflow checks into product design early in the development cycle (Compliance-by-Design).
Pilot feature rollout with two specific high-value clients to test 'stickiness' metrics before wider release.
execution_plan.success_metric: Increase in Annual Contract Value (ACV) from 3 key accounts by 15% due to specialized module adoption.
milestones: Successful beta test with defined user group.
Formal inclusion of new sticky feature into Q4 roadmap.

opportunities.title: Institutionalize Post-Merger Operational Excellence & Governance
opportunities.rationale: The recent merger created significant process duplication and structural fragility. A bold overhaul of core business processes (CRM, HRIS, Billing) is necessary to realize economies of scale and stabilize the operating model before market consolidation pressures intensify.

first_actions: Establish a centralized 'Integration Process Blueprint' committee involving leadership from all merged entities.
Conduct mandatory cross-functional training focused on compliance implications of new standardized processes (e.g., data handling, invoicing).
Prioritize the consolidation and retirement roadmap for redundant core systems.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction of reported operational process conflicts (e.g., billing discrepancies) by 40% within the first year.
milestones: Consolidated core system architecture defined and approved.
Single source of truth (SSOT) for customer data established.
Process Blueprint documentation signed off across all departments.

next_steps.action: Form a dedicated 'Process Harmonization Task Force' chartered with creating the single source of truth for critical operational workflows (sales-to-cash).
Host a mandatory, multi-department workshop focused on regulatory requirements and compliance gaps created by system overlaps.
Formalize the funding request process for innovation initiatives, moving away from ad-hoc committee requests towards a structured ROI and impact scoring model.
next_steps.owner: Head of Strategy / Innovation Squad Lead

key_weaknesses: Cultural integration remains fragile following the merger, leading to change fatigue and resistance in adopting standardized processes.
Significant process duplication and redundant core systems are creating major operational friction.
The formal decision-making committee structure slows down mid-cycle innovation funding despite successful agile adoption.

improvements: Successful adoption of Agile methodology, resulting in a 60% reduction in release cycle time and improved engineering collaboration.
Expanded market footprint through new enterprise clients and adjacent market penetration, demonstrating increased resilience.
Innovation team has maintained consistent progress on defined milestones despite corporate complexity.
persistent_gaps: The structural overlap of core systems (CRM, HR) continues to introduce manual workarounds and data inconsistencies.
Cultural integration efforts are hampered by the sheer volume of necessary process standardization required post-merger.
Innovation funding remains dependent on navigating complex, multi-stakeholder formal committee approvals.
achieved_milestones: Successful implementation of 2-week sprint cycles and continuous deployment practices.
Securing 8 new enterprise clients across expanded market segments.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The company has successfully stabilized its technical execution (agile adoption) and shown market expansion post-merger. However, operational complexity and internal governance issues have become the primary drag on scalability, shifting focus from product capability to structural process redesign.
